title: Position 1 device and receive-path characterization
goal: Determine receiver settings, host capture limits and basic sample integrity before RF room-mapping experiments.
hypothesis: The extended configuration accepts wide RX settings, but the USB host path imposes a lower continuous throughput ceiling.

environment.antennas: Standard supplied TX and RX antennas attached, per user
environment.operator: Seated near antennas; may move or leave. Movement timing and positions not logged.
environment.power: USB data connection observed; complete power wiring not independently inspected

protocol: Read live IIO device identity, ranges and initial state.
Power down TX LO, maximize TX attenuation, zero/disable DDS; verify before and after captures.
Capture six sample rates from 2.5 to 61.44 MS/s; measure delivery and sticky RX FIFO overflow.
Check manual RX gain settings 20/40/60 dB qualitatively with ambient input.
Repeat 2.5 MS/s for approximately ten seconds.
Check 5/6/7 MS/s throughput boundary; repeat 5 MS/s for 13.4 seconds.
Restore initial RX settings, retain TX mute and verify raw-data hashes.
code_provenance: Exact capture source snapshots stored beside each run, matching script_sha256. Analysis source is versioned in Git.
failures: RX FIFO overflow at 7, 10, 20, 30.72 and 61.44 MS/s; these captures must not be treated as continuous.
suspected_causes: Host transport pipeline saturates around 6.45 MS/s. The individual contributions of USB, RNDIS, device CPU and host are not isolated.
uncertainties: Sample continuity not certified by a known test sequence or hardware timestamps.
Reference source and absolute clock accuracy unverified.
Actual analog filter response, noise figure and gain accuracy uncalibrated.
Ambient radio traffic and operator motion are uncontrolled.
One fixed pair has no independent bearing observation.
next_tests: Receive-only spectrum occupancy survey at position 1.
A controlled source or RX-internal test sequence to validate continuity more strongly if needed.
TX/RX timing and leakage calibration only in a suitable transmit interval, respecting the user exclusions.
A known target displacement before interpreting measured changes as geometry.
